name: Question 3
worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}-4 \\  & ={X}^{2}-4I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(D)={D}^{2}-4I.$ 

Let's calculate ${D}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{2} & =D\cdot D \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -6 & -4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -6 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(D):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(D) & ={D}^{2}-4I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4-4 & 0+0 \\ 0+0 & 4-4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Consider the matrix D=[42−6−4]. Find f(D) if f(X)=X2−4.

a
[1001]
b
[21−3−2]
c
[0000]
d
[42−6−4]
e
[2−31−2]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

f(X)=X2−4=X2−4I

So, we want to find f(D)=D2−4I.

Let's calculate D2 as follows: D2=D⋅D=[42−6−4]⋅[42−6−4]=[4004]

Now, we can evaluate f(D):

f(D)=D2−4I=[4004]−4[1001]=[4004]+[−400−4]=[4−40+00+04−4]=[0000]
